description: Every syllabic corpus word (2+ signs) with no proposed reading in the lexicon, translations or onomasticon, with its attestations, a status and a note on the edition's text. Hand-edited. `surface_damage` maps each attestation whose Unicode word carries the damage marker to where it sits (start / interior / end); it records damaged surface, not necessarily lost signs, so an edge-damaged word may be incomplete.

statuses.role_only: classed by role only (onomasticon type or translation label), no reading
statuses.edge_overlap: a lexicon word sits at one edge; often a chance 2-sign overlap

excluded.NU-MA-RE: corpus splits *28B-NU-MA-RE (ZA4a, ZA5b, ZA15a); the word is lexicon JI-NU-MA-RE
excluded.JA-SA-SA-RA-MA: corpus breaks the line after MA on KNZa10; the word is lexicon JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA
excluded.TE-TA-NA-MA-JE: corpus runs TE-TA-NA-MA-JE as one word on PE6; translations read TE + TA-NA-MA-JE
excluded.WA-DI-NI: corpus runs WA-DI-NI as one word on HTWc3007, HTWc3008; GORILA prints WA · DI-NI on 3008a; the word is lexicon DI-NI
excluded.A-NA-TI-*301-WA-JA: broken at both ends on IOZa8; translations read ]A-NA-TI-*301-WA-JA[ as ʿAnatī nawaya

entries.note: A personal name: recipient with a numeral on six tablets at two sites (HT 118 pigs, PH(?) 31a with *21M, HT 3 and HT 97a beside other names, HT 85b in a one-unit roster after WA-DU-NI-MI). Linear B ma-di is a man on the Knossos roster KN As(1) 603.2 (VIR 1) and on the sheep tablet KN Db 1168. Cf. Hurrian mad=i 'wisdom' (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 102), at Nuzi chiefly a final name element, Enna-mati, Tešup-mati (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 234, 265), beside Matija and a broken Ma-ti-… (ibid., s.vv. MATIJA, MATI . . .). No reading.

Heads HT18 (GRA+QE 20, OLE+KI 2, *304 3) and the second section of HT27b (*591, SA 4, RE 70); never carries its own quantity. PA-SE-JA is the same base with -JA. The anointer (√p-š-š) and protectress (√p-s-ḥ) etymologies are withdrawn: the context selects neither, and pāset needs both ḥ and feminine -t unwritten. No reading.

Always TA-I-*123 (LB AROM) and always a recipient: HT9a (between *324-DI-RA and A-RU), HT9b (between QE-PU and DI-NA-U, I dotted, GORILA I 19) and the head of HT39 with KU-RE-JU and SA-MA-TI. The HT9b entry sits inside the wine total (3+3+8+2+2+2+4 = KU-RO 24), so *123 tags the recipient, not the commodity, cf. LB PN + a-re-pa-zo-o 'unguent-boiler' + AROM (PY Un 249.2). No reading.

One of the recurring HT units: on HT13 it takes 56 of the wine total 130½ beside TE-KI, KU-ZU-NI and DA-SI-*118, the set HT85a counts in men (TE-KE for TE-KI). It is a single entry in the lists HT7a (.5 after DA-RE, TE over an erasure, GORILA I 15) and HT85b (.2–3 TE-TU[ ] 1, between PA and KA, the lacuna perhaps hiding no sign, GORILA I 133). No reading.

A heading, never a recipient: it opens both oil sections of HT140, each followed by a name (*86-SI-NI, *86-SI-*118-KA), the second with a partial lacuna after SI (GORILA I 237), and the grain account HT15 (684, 570, KI-RO 400). SigLA reads *34 secure on both. No reading.

HT Wa 1029 and Wa 1030 are nodules with one *301 on face α and one on face γ, filed under nodules with two signs (GORILA II 9). The two signs stand on different faces and form no sign group. Not a word.

KH Wc 2054 and Wc 2055, roundels: GORILA III 134 prints both as facsimiles only, with no transcription. Each carries one incised figure, a vertical stroke with a zigzag joined to a hooked sign, which Younger reads as the single ligature logogram *301̣+MỊ (*605), both components dotted, in the logogram column, with 5̣ and 6 seal impressions (Younger, Linear A Texts). A logogram on a receipt, not a sign group. Not a word.

Both attestations are damaged. KH102, a 2.5 × 1.6 cm LM I fragment, preserves two signs in part, A and 'presumably MI' (Hallager et al. 2014, PoDIA 7: 216, Fig. 11). PH14b (MM IIB lame) is retrograde: A-MỊ-[, MI dotted and broken after it (GORILA I 305 prints ]-MỊ-A in left-to-right order, Younger A-MI-[), so A-MI may begin a longer word (cf. A-MI-DA-O, A-MI-TA). Not readable.
Must recipient at two sites: ARKH2 KU-RA *131B 5 ∥ ZA10b DU-RE-ZA-SE *131B 5, and ZA20 closes on KU-RA 130 against 26 visible (GORILA III 7, 193). No reading.

Both attestations are damaged. HT39 .3 KU-RẸ[, between SA-MA-TI 10 and KU-RO, RE dotted, broken after, no numeral (GORILA I 75). HT53b .4 ]KỤ-RE[, broken on both sides, KU dotted (GORILA I 103). Either may belong to a longer word: KU-RE-JU (HT39, HT117b), QA-KU-RE, QE-KU-RE. Not readable.

Recipient in two Haghia Triada lists that also share DI. HT85b (Scribe 9, Casa Room 7): QE-KA 1 among the single entries under KI-KI-RA-JA, after KI-RE-TA₂ 1, with DI 1 and ME-ZA 1 (GORILA I 133). HT111a .2 ]QE-KA 8, broken before, above QA-SẠ-[, ]QẠ-RU 8 and DI 14[ (GORILA I 181). No reading.

MA 2b .1 ]-RE-TI 4, broken before RE, the word running into the break (GORILA I 271). MI Zb 3, a jug handle, has no printed reading: Younger lists it as an inscription of doubtful status (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Not readable.

ZA 26a .1 SI-TE · DI-DI-[, the first group of the tablet, the logogram and 13 following at the head of .2 (GORILA III 202–203). Intact and undotted on both copies, SI drawn as hatched uprights between two arcs, unlike the SI of ZA 20 SI-TE-TU. The editors draw TE with two short bars on each side of the stem and allow that the stroke after it is the numeral 1, not a divider. MIL Zb 3, the second witness, breaks through SI (photograph and facsimile), and Younger gives no text for it: he prints MIL Zb 1 alone for Miletos and reports the rest unpublished (Younger, Linear A Texts). SI-TE also stands inside SI-TE-TU (ZA 20), QE-SI-TE (MA Ze 11) and KE-SI-TE (KN Ze 49). As a tablet heading it compares with a place: the Kom el-Hetan list ends with a damaged oval, restored [sȝ]-i-tȝ-[y] and tentatively identified as Siteia (Cline & Stannish 2011, 10). No reading.

ZA 6a .3 I-SẸ[, SE dotted, broken after, OLIV after the break (GORILA III 157). ZA 6a .9 ]20 I-SE at the end of the line, before .10 [·][, which the tabular copy joins to it as I-SE-[ (GORILA III 157). Not readable.

HT 37 .1 KA-KỊ · SU[, KI dotted, after MI+JA+I · (GORILA I 71). HT 37 .5 KA-KI 11, KA dotted in the copie tabulaire and drawn damaged in the copie normalisée (GORILA I 71). A sign is dotted or damaged on each witness. Not readable.

THE Zg 15, a discoid clay loom weight from Akrotiri (Pillar Pit 66P, early MM III), signs incised before firing. The report gives Karnava's reading AB 164a-53-01 and states that difficulties of reading leave doubts (Del Freo, Rapport 2016–2021, 106). RILA-S1 lists the piece among its doubtful inscriptions (D 26). *164 has no resolved value. Not readable.
HT 26b .4 *188̣-*86 7̣[, *188 dotted, the numeral dotted and broken after, above the broken lower edge, after Ị-*308̣ 2[ (GORILA I 47). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PSE Zb 1, a pithos shoulder fragment from Pseira (LM IB), broken at the right. Younger prints *188-DU-SE[ with DU and SE marked doubtful and reports Floyd's alternatives *188-A-I[ and *188-WA-I, the second and third signs doubtful in each (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 62 .3 *28B-TI-[·] 6, a sign lost after TI (GORILA I 117). Not readable.
HT 94b .6 *21F-TU-[·] 1[, a sign lost after TU and a trace after the numeral (GORILA I 153). GORILA's note offers *21F-TU-NẸ. Not readable.

KH 5 .3 WI-NA-DU · *301̣-NA ·, *301 dotted on the copie normalisée, the apparatus finding L48b a less satisfactory reading of the sign (GORILA III 25). Younger marks *301 doubtful and sets *301-NA in the logogram column (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.

ZA 6a .1 *305-WA-NA *171 19, the first entry of face a, *34-JU-TE-MI[ following across .1–2 (GORILA III 157). Intact, no dots, and Younger prints the same (Younger, Linear A Texts). *305 has only a CANDIDATE value /ḏa/, and the logogram *171 after it has no reading, so the slot is unknown. No reading.

HT122b .2 *306-KI-TA₂ 7, all three signs whole and undotted at the head of the line, a trace after the numeral. .1 breaks off after VIR+[. GORILA's tabular copy sets ] before the word (GORILA I 209), but the drawing and the photograph show the left edge whole beside *306, and a crack crosses the line at KI (GORILA I 208). Sole attestation. No reading.

SigLA's reading of KH21 line 3, which Younger's table follows. GORILA III 55 prints ]*306 1̣0̣0̣: broken before *306, a circle read as 100 with undetermined marks inside, traces after it, vest.[ below. Younger compares the circle to a Hieroglyphic group-of-number sign. GORILA prints no QE or DU, so the word may be *306 plus a numeral. Not readable.
TY 2 .2 *309-DA-PỤ-[·] 10, DA set on *309, PU dotted, a sign lost after PU and an erasure after the numeral (GORILA I 324–325). Not readable.

TY 2 .2–3 PA-DA-*309-RU-JU-KI 100: PA ends line 2, DA opens line 3, RU is written above *309, and the tabular copy sets the six signs as one entry with no divider (GORILA I 325). SigLA orders ru before *309. Every other syllabic entry on the tablet opens with *309, so this is a *309 entry with PA-DA before it, not a name. Not a word.
TY 2 .3 *309+RI-JU[, RI joined to *309, broken after JU (GORILA I 325). Not readable.
TY 2 .5 *309-RI-[·]-WẠ-JU, RI the AB53 hook on *309, a sign lost after it and WA dotted (GORILA I 325). Not readable.

HT 10b .2 *312-TA 6½, after TA-RI-NA 15 and before KA-SA-RU 6, the side over an erasure (GORILA I 21). Whole and undotted. *312 is the flax logogram at CANDIDATE, and the syllable KI it is given inside words is SPECULATIVE, so no reading can rest on it. No reading.
Intact, after VIN+KA 10 at the end of line 2, before GRA+PA 40[ on line 3 (GORILA III 159), the slot of I-KU-JU-TI-*28B on line 1. *312 has no resolved syllabic value. No reading.

PH 9a, the only group on the face, followed by a fraction sign, on a pierced MM II tablet from Vano 25 whose other face carries a vessel logogram and numerals (GORILA I 298). Intact and undotted on both copies. *317 is a logogram candidate (LIQḤU, CANDIDATE) and *353 has no value, so two of the three signs are unresolved. No reading.
HT 94a .4 *318-*306 11, whole and undotted, after a numeral at the broken left edge and before the CYP and NI entries (GORILA I 151). *318 has no value. No reading.

HT 11a .3 *322-RI 1, RI written small at the upper right of *322, before KU-RO 10 (GORILA I 23). The copie normalisée leaves both signs undotted, the copie tabulaire dots *322. *322 has no syllabic value, and its logogram value PIRRI 'fruit' is SPECULATIVE and takes its final -ri from this very word, so it cannot read it. No reading.

HT 96a .4 PI-TA-RA · 1 *323 *344 1, the second half of the line over an erasure, *344 with small signs above and below it (GORILA I 157). The copie tabulaire sets *323 and *344 in the two logogram columns, as it sets *323 and *317 on .3. Two logograms, not a sign group. Not a word.

HT 119 .4–5 *327-JU 8, whole and undotted, after *306-TU 2 and before KU-RO 160 (GORILA I 203). *327 heads the tablet as a logogram with 34 (.1) and has no syllabic value. HT 97a counts *327 33 and JU 15 as separate entries: *327-JU joins the two categories, as VIR+KA qualifies VIR on the same tablet. Not a name. No reading.
ZA 6a .1–2 *34-JU-TE-MI[, *34-JU at the end of .1 after *305-WA-NA *171 19, TE-MI at the start of .2, broken after MI, ]1̣80 after the break (GORILA III 157). Sole attestation. Not readable.
TY 2 .1 *309B-[ ]-PU-PI 5̣00, the sign set above *309B lost, the hundreds dotted, PI dotted in the tabular copy (GORILA I 324–325). The *34 is SigLA's. Not readable.

PH 10, an MM II tablet from Vano 25, the only group, followed by a logogram and two fraction signs (GORILA I 299). Undotted. *355 and *354 have no values, so the group has one resolved sign. No reading.

HT 24b .2 *539 *118 1, after ]*118 1¾ (.1, one sign lost on the left) and SI+ME-KI 1¾ (.1–2) (GORILA I 43). The copie tabulaire sets *539 as the entry and *118 in the logogram column before the numeral in all three entries. *118 is the commodity. Not a word.

HT 38 .2–3 *554 at the end of .2, then *118 3 at the head of .3, before TELA+KU 2 (GORILA I 73). The copie tabulaire sets *554 apart and *118 in the logogram column before 3, as on HT 24b. Not a word.

KH Wc 2065, roundel: GORILA III 138 prints a facsimile only, with no transcription. Younger reads the incised figure as the ligature logogram *301+*351 (*607), in the logogram column, with two seal impressions (Younger, Linear A Texts). A logogram on a receipt, not a sign group. Not a word.

KH Wc 2123, roundel found out of context in a Geometric levelling deposit: the editors read [[A 373, PI-KA]], all three signs erased before the seal impressions, the first an isolated bird-shaped sign they number A 373 and tentatively take for a new sign and an ideogram, set apart from PI-KA (Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, 13–14, Fig. 5). Del Freo and Zurbach tentatively take A 373 for a variant of the tripod logogram (Del Freo, Rapport 2016–2021, 100). The listed group joins the isolated sign to PI-KA. Not a word.
HT 140 .2 *86̣-SỊ-*118-KA 3, *86 and SI dotted, after U-*34-SI (GORILA I 237). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 140 .1 *86-SỊ-NI · 1̣[ ], SI dotted, the numeral dotted and broken after it, after U-*34-SI : (GORILA I 237). The apparatus allows NI to be the logogram. Sole attestation. Not readable.

MA 1a, a three-sided bar from the Malia palace: X, then I-DU-WI · *47 · QE-DE-MI-NU · (GORILA I 268–269). The copie normalisée sets X apart from I-DU-WI, Younger prints X as the mark that opens the bar, and face b opens directly with A-MA · *47 · QE-DE-MI-NU (Younger, Linear A Texts). The word is I-DU-WI, and the listed form fuses the opening mark with it. Not a word.

HT 96a .2, the third heading group after I-TI-TI-KU-NI · A-PA-RA-NE, over a grain list (GORILA I 157). HT 96b has QA-*118-RA-RE in the same slot after A-PA-RA-NE. *123 is LB AROM and has no syllabic value; cf. TA-I-*123 (HT9a, HT9b, HT39). Intact. No reading.
KH58 .5 A-*301[, signs undotted, broken after *301, following a damaged CYP entry and ½ (GORILA III 81). The group may continue, as A-*301-KI-TA-A (TYZb4) does. Sole attestation. Not readable.

TY Zb 4, pithos, below the rim, the only text: A-*301̣-KI-TA-A, *301 dotted on both copies, an erasure [[ ]] between A and *301 (GORILA IV 109). Younger records the same erasure (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.

TY 3a .5 Ạ-DA OLE+U 21, A dotted on both copies, the first entry below the ruling under .4, before a second oil entry broken at the right (GORILA I 327). Younger marks A doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH83 .1 A-DI-NE[, signs undotted, broken after NE, preceded by an unidentified trace at the left break (GORILA III 99). The tablet is a palimpsest (GORILA III 98). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KH4 .1 A-DU-RE[, signs undotted, broken after RE; .2 *306 4, CYP and a fraction (GORILA III 25). The same *306 4 and CYP entry follows A-DU-[·]-ZA on KH 11 .3, where the apparatus finds A-DU-RE-ZA possible (GORILA III 39). Not readable.

KH 11 .1 A-DU-[·]-ZA, CYP and a fraction, the third sign lost; the apparatus finds A-DU-RE-ZA possible (GORILA III 39). It heads issues of cyperus, SU, wine and *306; .3 *306 4 and CYP follow A-DU-RE[ on KH 4 .2 as well (GORILA III 25). On HT 88 .1, A-DU VIR+KA 20 is followed by RE-ZA 6, RE over an erasure (GORILA I 139). Not readable.

HT115b .4 A-Ị-[··] 1̣, I dotted, two signs lost after it inside the word, the numeral dotted (GORILA I 191). GORILA's note restores the two lost signs only with doubt. A-I is the start of a longer word. Not readable.

IO Za <1>, a limestone votive ladle from the Juktas summit sanctuary, the inscription painted inside it, now lost and never seen by GORILA. Evans found it damaged by fire, with two legible signs and traces of a third (PM I 623–624, fig. 461). Younger prints A-JE-SA with SA marked doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). The third sign rests on traces. Not readable.

entries.translation_label: unread—vowel+JU carries ≤1 consonant, nothing survives the null model; hinges on the standalone-JU value dispute
entries.note: HT Zd 155, a graffito on stucco, A-JU · NA-MA-MA-TI-TI-A319, A-JU whole and undotted before the divider (GORILA IV 131). No reading.

PA 1 .1–2 A-KU-JU-PA-*118 35, the only entry on a small tablet from Papoura (GORILA I 284). Undotted on the copie normalisée. The copie tabulaire dots JU, as it dots JU on PH 2 .3 (GORILA I 289) and not on ZA 14 .2 QA-TI-JU (GORILA III 181). *118 closes the group directly before the numeral, the position in which it stands alone as a unit logogram, and GORILA prints no division. No reading.
TY 3a .7 A-KU-TU-*361[, broken after *361, traces after the break in the editors' note (GORILA I 327). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH53 ]Ạ-ME-*123 · NE[, broken before A, A dotted, NE broken after (GORILA III 77). A-ME may be the end of a longer word. Sole attestation. Not readable.
PH(?)31b .5 ]A-MI-DA-O *21M 1[, broken before A and after the numeral (GORILA I 319). Not readable.
ZA Zg 35, a bone label: ]A-MI-JA-RU · SE-WA-AU-DE, broken before the first sign, which is A in the facsimile (Younger ]ME). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT126a .2 A-NA-[·] 1̣, a sign lost after NA inside the word, the numeral dotted, then Ụ[ (GORILA I 217). GORILA's note: a pebble makes the lost sign hard to identify. A-NA is the start of a longer word. Not readable.

PE Zb ]A-NU[, a sherd in Heraklion broken on both sides (Younger, Linear A Texts). Younger gives no inventory number or publication citation for the piece. Both signs are legible, only the edges are broken. No reading.

HT 14 .3 A-PỤ₂-NA-DU GRA 47, PU₂ dotted in the copie normalisée, at the head of the second set of entries (GRA, OLE+MI, OLE+DI, *304, OLIV) (GORILA I 29). The copie tabulaire prints PU₂ without the dot. Sole attestation. Not readable.
Left edge broken (GORILA I 177): signs may be lost before A-RA-JU. Not readable.
HT122b .3 A-RA-JU-U-DE-ZẠ, ZA dotted, the numeral partly restored, at the head of the line after .2 breaks off (GORILA I 209). The ending matches U-DE-ZA (HT122a .1). Sole attestation. Not readable.
GORILA IV 158–159 prints this sixteen-sign bronze-bowl inscription without dividers and dots the initial A, RA, and KO. TO-MA-RO is a CANDIDATE personal-name segment. Not readable.
KH 5 .1 A-DA-KI-SI-KA · A-RA-U-DA ·, the heading (GORILA III 25). SI-KA at its end matches the HT nodule word. No reading.
THE Zb 4 ]A-RẸ[, broken on both sides, RE dotted, and the note allows A-SẠ[ instead (GORILA IV 105). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 28a .5 A-RU-DA-RA GRA 5 *304 2, whole and undotted, at the head of the line in the A-SI-JA-KA list (GORILA I 53). A recipient of grain. No reading.

Roundel face a, one word over three lines, A-SA / SỤ-MA / I-SẸ (GORILA II 2). SU and SE are dotted. A-SA- also opens A-SA-DA-KA (MA Wc 5, a roundel), A-SA-RA₂ (HT 89) and A-SA-SA-RA-ME (IO Zb 10). Not readable.
HT 9b .2–3 Ạ-SỊ 3, both signs dotted, after PẠ-DẸ 3 (GORILA I 19). The apparatus does not exclude A-RU, the entry HT 9a .5–6 lists in the same sequence (A-RU 4¼). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KH 99, published as KH 98: the editors print .2 ]A-SI-*118 and .3 ]KU-KA-[, two groups on two lines, both broken at the left and the second at the right (Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, 10–11, Fig. 3). The listed form joins them. Not a word.
Intact on ARKH 2 lines .2–3 (GORILA III 7), A-SI-DA-TO-I 12, a recipient in the must list headed SI-DA-TE. No reading.

KH 9 .1 A-SI-SU-PO-A · VIR+*307[, heading a list of small fractional issues of figs, cyperus, wine and *304, the logogram dotted and broken at the right (GORILA III 35). Intact, no dots; a divider after the last A, nothing before the first. A heading: a name, place or occasion. Valério (2016, 224 n. 518) sets it beside A-SU-PU-WA (ARKH 2) and LB su-pu-wo (KN C 912). A split A-SI SU-PO-A, after I-SI · *303+D on .3, has no divider. No reading.
KH39 .1 A-TA-[, signs undotted, the hyphen before the break marking a group that went on (GORILA III 67). A-TA- opens several longer words, at Khania A-TA-*350 (KH11). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KH 11 .5 A-TA-*350, then *301 1 at the head of .6 (GORILA III 39). Intact, no dots. *350 occurs nowhere else and has no value. Younger prints A-TE-*350 and compares A-TA-*301- of the libation formula (Younger, Linear A Texts), and GORILA reads TA. No reading.
Intact, dividers both sides, first entry under KI-RA: A-TA-RE · NI ½ (GORILA III 165), in a list of names with quantities. No reading.

KH 11 .4 A-TO-*349-TỌ-I, the second TO dotted, the copie tabulaire dotting I as well, written over traces of an erasure, then an erased CYP and CYP+E, its quantity 3 on .5 (GORILA III 39). *349 occurs nowhere else (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
GORILA I 137 .5 A-RA-[·]-A-TU 1̣, the third sign lost, no divider. GORILA's alternative reads two entries, A-RA-[·] 1̣ and A-TU 1̣. Not readable.

KH 97 as listed, A7092 A306 A707 BOSm, matches GORILA's KH 87 down to the dimensions: a damaged *306 ends .2 and the fraction J begins .3, before BOSm 1[ (GORILA III 100–101). The published KH 97 is another document (Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, 8–9, Fig. 2). A306-A707 joins a logogram to a fraction across the line break. Not a word.
KH 103 reads three logograms, A303 being the cyperus logogram (*303 in Younger's Khania transcriptions), followed by VIN. A run of logograms, not a sign group. Not a word.
The end of A-[·]-DA-*118 (GORILA IV 168). Not a word.
GORILA I 218–219 reads ]*304+PA-DA-*47-KU[ as one group, alternatively ]*629-DA-*47-KU[. No divider licenses DA-*47-KU as an independent word. Not readable.
TY 2 .4 *309C-DA-[·]-JU 17[, DA-[·]-JU set above *309C, the middle sign lost, the numeral broken after 17 (GORILA I 324–325). Not readable.

HT6b .5 DẠ-KỊ 3¼, both signs dotted, on a palimpsest face (.1–6 over an erasure, GORILA I 13). HT123+124a .6 reads DA-TU, not DA-KI (GORILA I 211; SigLA's DA-KI misreads TU). No clean witness. Not readable.
HT123+124a .6 DA-TU OLIV 15, the fourth of four olive-and-oil entries (GORILA I 211). Intact: DA (AB01) and TU (AB69), not the KI of KI-RO on .2, .5, .7; SigLA prints DA-KI. No reading.

SE Zf 1, a bronze double axe from Selakanos near Kato Symi (Ashmolean AE 85). Younger prints DA-KU with both signs marked doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). The piece, published by Raison and Pope (1994), lies outside both GORILA and RILA-S1. Not readable.

PH 7b .2 ]DA-RA L, broken before DA, a trace to the left in the editors' note (GORILA I 295). PH 7a .4 has JA-SI-DA-RẠ[, RA dotted and broken after (GORILA I 295). Sole attestation of the listed form. Not readable.
ZA 18a .1 DA-RE-KU[, broken after, traces before the divider (GORILA III 191). Not readable.

HT 38 .2 *403VAS with DA-RO-PA ligatured above it, 1, below the vestigia of .1 (GORILA I 73). The third sign has an oblique stroke, and the apparatus reads PA only if the stroke is accidental, and then dotted (DA-RO-PẠ). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 7b .2 DA-RU-*329 2, whole and undotted, after *21F-TU-NE 1, both lines over an erasure (GORILA I 15). *329 has no value. No reading.
HT 94b .2 DE-DI 1, whole and undotted, in the list headed KI-RO ·, after PA-TA-NE 1 and before KE-KI-RU 1 (GORILA I 153). No reading.
HT 94b .5 *86 · RA-[·]-DẸ-ME-TE 1, a sign lost after RA and DE dotted (GORILA I 153). GORILA's note offers RA-RỊ-DẸ-ME-PA. Not readable.
ARKH 4b .3 ]DE-MI 10, broken before DE (GORILA III 15). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT11b .1 ]DẸ-NỤ, broken before, DE and NU dotted, followed by a stroke that GORILA's tabular copy gives as 1̣ (GORILA I 23). The editors give ]DE-PẠ₃ as less likely. Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT Wc 3017 face a QA-KU-RE · DI-*306 ·, face b CYP+D · *304+PA (GORILA II 77). DI-*306 whole and undotted between dividers. No reading.
HT86b is an erased copy of HT86a's opening entries, A-KA-RU, KU-NI-SU, SA-RU, then ⟦DI-DE⟧ where a.3 has DI-DE-RU 20. The draft stops after DE (GORILA I 135, Younger, Linear A Texts). Not a word.

ZA 26a .1 SI-TE · DI-DI-[, the second DI without its upper horizontal stroke, the word running on into the break (GORILA III 203). The word may continue as DI-DI-KO-RA-ME-TA₂ (ZA 11a), DI-DI-KA-SE (ZA Zb 3) or DI-DI-ZA-KE (HT 1). Sole attestation. Not readable.

ZA 11a .1 DI-DI-KO-RA-ME⌊ ⌋TA₂ · *516 · GRA+PA, all six syllabograms undotted, a small destroyed space before TA₂ that the editors say could have held a word divider (GORILA III 173). Segmentation unresolved. Sole attestation. No reading.

HT 1 .2–3 DỊ-DI-ZA-KE 52, the first DI dotted, its stem in a worn patch on the facsimile, DI-DI at the end of .2 after ZU-SU 70 and ZA-KE on .3 (GORILA I 3, facsimile I 2). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT29 .3 DI-JA-I 2, all three signs whole and undotted at the head of the line, the whole of .1–6 written over an erasure, JA perhaps over a further one. .2 breaks off after PA-JA-RE 1̣[, and GORILA's tabular copy sets ] before the word (GORILA I 55). Sole attestation. No reading.
HT52a .2 DI-KA-KỊ[, after the numeral 4, KI dotted, broken after (GORILA I 101). GORILA's note gives DI-KA-TỤ[ as less probable. Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 27 .2 ]DI-KI 2, broken before DI, below sup. mut. and a line of vestiges. The editors ask whether DI-KI is complete (GORILA III 205). Sole attestation. Not readable.
PH 1a .1 ]DI-RA-DI-NA *316, broken before the first DI (GORILA I 287). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH6 .1 ]CYP+D ½ DI-SI-[, signs undotted, the hyphen before the break marking a group that went on (GORILA III 27). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 22 .4 DỤ-JỤ[, after the numeral 6, both signs dotted, broken after (GORILA III 199). Sole attestation. Not readable.
MI 2 .2 ]DỤ-KA[, broken on both sides, DU dotted, and the note allows ]KỤ-KA[ (GORILA V 57). Sole attestation. Not readable.
Complete, HT 123+124b line 5: DU-MA-I-NA ⅜ in the terebinth list, written over an erasure, I dotted (GORILA I 213). Not readable.

HT127a .2 DU-NE-MI 1̣[, all three signs whole and undotted at the head of the line, the numeral dotted and broken after, erasures passim on .1–5. .1 is vest.[, and GORILA's tabular copy sets ] before the word (GORILA I 219). Sole attestation. No reading.
MA 10b .1 ]DỤ-PỊ-TE-WA, broken before DU, DU and PI dotted, a divider and a vessel logogram with 1 after (GORILA V 52–53). Sole attestation. Not readable.
MA 2a .1 ]DU-RA 5, broken before DU (GORILA I 271). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KH20 .4 ]DỤ-RE-ZA · CYP+E ½ NI ¼, broken before DU, DU dotted (GORILA III 53). The apparatus finds ]SẸ-RE-ZA not entirely impossible. Khania also has A-DU-RE[ (KH 4) and A-DU-[·]-ZA (KH 11), both heading cyperus entries; Zakros has DU-RE-ZA-SE (ZA 10a, 10b, 20). Not readable.

ZA 10a .5 DU-RE-ZA-SE 2 closes a list opened by TA-NA-TE and A-TA-NA-TE; ZA 10b .1–2 DU-RE-ZA-SE *131B 5 stands where ARKH 2 has KU-RA *131B 5; ZA 20 .1–2 ]DU-RẸ-ZA-SE[, broken at both ends, RE dotted, GORILA allowing a join with ]MI[ on .2, with KU-RA on the same tablet (GORILA III 168–171, 193). At Khania ]DU-RE-ZA (KH 20), A-DU-RE[ (KH 4) and A-DU-[·]-ZA (KH 11) head cyperus entries. No reading.
PH(?) 31b .2 ]-DỤ-RI *22M 1, broken before DU, the word running into the break, DU dotted (GORILA I 319). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT4 .2 ]-DU-RỊ-TE 2̣, broken before with the word running into the break, RI dotted, the numeral dotted (GORILA I 9). GORILA's note allows ]SỤ-DU-RỊ-TE or ]TẠ-DU-RỊ-TE. Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT36 .2 DU-ZU-WA at the end of the line after the 44 ½ of the .1 heading JE-DI … GRA+QE, all three signs whole and undotted, its numeral 7 ½ on .3, written over an erasure with one unit dotted (GORILA I 69). Sole attestation. No reading.

HT Wa 1026 is a nodule with one sign on each of two faces, a hooked sign on α (read E), with damage at its foot, and *301 on γ, filed by GORILA under nodules with two signs (GORILA II 9). The faces give no reading order. The same page has *301 alone on a face of Wa 1025, 1029 and 1030, and Wa 1027 KA / SI against Wa 1028 SI / KA. The listed form joins two separate marks into one group. Not a word.
PE 1 .3–4 E-KA[ VIR 72, broken after KA (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 11a .3 ]E-KU-RU 2̣, broken before E, the numeral dotted and the fraction on .4 (GORILA III 173). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 1b .1 E-MỊ[, MI dotted, broken after, traces of signs after MI and before ]RỌ (GORILA I 333). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PH Wg 45 (formerly PH Wc 45), an MM II nodule from Vano 25. GORILA's drawing shows the strokes as broken outlines (GORILA II 96). Younger marks all three signs doubtful and calls the reading very doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). Not readable.
End not secure: partial lacuna after RI (GORILA III 175). Not readable.

HT26b .4 Ị *3̣0̣8̣ 2̣, I and *308 both dotted and the numeral dotted, at the head of the last preserved line above inf. mut. GORILA's tabular copy sets I in the ideogram column and *308 in a column of its own (GORILA I 47). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH32 .1 I-*3̣3̣1̣[, *331 dotted, broken after it, written over an erasure, above 5[ (GORILA III 63). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ARKH 4b .3 I-*47[, broken after *47 at the end of the line, the numeral 9 at the head of .4 (GORILA III 15). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 11b .2b ] I-DE[, in signs of larger module below .2a, broken after DE, a break before I with a space between (GORILA III 175). Sole attestation. Not readable.
IO Za 14 SI-]RU-TE · I-DI-[, broken after DI, the word running into the break (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.

IO Za 5 (HM 3643, stone lamp(?), Iouktas): ]I-JA-RE-DI-JA · I-JA-PA[, broken after PA (GORILA V 23). Longer forms: I-JA-PA-ME (KH 7a, in a VIR list); in the libation texts I-NA-JA-PA-QA (PK Za 11) and JA-PA-QA (PK Za 12, last word). No restoration is secured. Not readable.

IO Za 5 (HM 3643, stone lamp(?), Iouktas): ]I-JA-RE-DI-JA · I-JA-PA[, broken before the first I (GORILA V 22–23). The fourth sign is damaged: GORILA reads DI, and the drawing also allows A. A clear divider follows the group, then I-JA-PA[ to the right break. The sequence JA-RE- recurs in I-NA-JA-RE-TA[ (AP Za 2 .2, a serpentine jar). Not readable.
HT49b .2 Ị-KỊ[ ]TẠ, I and KI dotted, broken after KI, TA beyond the lacuna, on a face GORILA calls entirely palimpsest (GORILA I 95). Sole attestation. Not readable.

THE Zg 16, a faience triton fragment from the House of the Benches at Akrotiri (excavated 2019), painted on the rim and unpublished. The report reads ]AB 78, AB 28-67-26-78 (]QE, I-KI-RU-QE) from a photograph: the second sign is followed by a small gap and is uncertain, AB 67 (KI) the report's preference and AB 81 (KU) its alternative (Del Freo, Rapport 2016–2021, 106–107). Not readable.
GORILA IV 5 reads AP Za 2 .1 ]-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE[, broken at both ends with a trace before KU, perhaps I. It is a form of KU-PA₃-NA-TU, its ending lost. Not readable.
KH18 .2 ]5̣ I-KU-PI[, numeral dotted, word signs undotted, broken after PI (GORILA III 49). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT35 .1 I-KU-TA at the end of the line after TI-TI-KU · *326 ·, all three signs whole and undotted, its entry CYP 1 at the head of .2 (GORILA I 67). Sole attestation. Linear B i-ku-to is a man in the dative at Mycenae, MY Oi 705.1 (DMic I); Woudhuizen 2016, 217 no. 14. No reading.
ZA 6b .5 I-MA[, below PA-ZA-[, broken after MA, traces after MA (GORILA III 159). Sole attestation. Not readable.
PH 54 .1 I-SA-RI-KE[ (AB 28-31-53-44[), broken after KE, the tablet broken on three sides (Militello, ASAtene 92, 2014, 159). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KN Ze 44 28-?-54-57, second sign unidentified (Owens, Minos 25/26, 367–69). Not readable.

PH 14a ]NỊ *304 JA⟦JA⟧ as printed left to right, NI dotted at the left break, JA and *304 whole and undotted, an erased JA beside JA (GORILA I 305). Younger reads the face retrograde as ]JA-*304 followed by FIC, JA written over an erased JA (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). GORILA V indexes *304 on PH 14a as an isolated sign and leaves grouping and direction open (GORILA V 138, 287). Sole attestation. No reading.
HT119 .4 JA-*345 10, both signs whole and undotted, a personnel entry between KU-PA₃-NA-TU 7, TI 7 and *306-TU 2 (GORILA I 203). *345 has no resolved value. Sole attestation. No reading.
ZA 26a .2 JA-KI[, after *21F 13, broken after KI (GORILA III 203). JA-KI-SI-KI-NU (ARKH Zf 9) begins the same way. Sole attestation. Not readable.
KN Za 17 ]-JA-QE ·, broken before JA, the word running into the break, a divider after QE (GORILA IV 11). Sole attestation. Not readable.

ARKH 1b .1 ]JA-RE 3̣[, broken before JA, the numeral dotted and broken after (GORILA III 5). JA-RE may be the end of a longer word: PA-JA-RE (HT 8b, HT 29, HT 88, ZA 10b), TE-JA-RE (HT 117a). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KN 32b .3 ]-JA-SU 1̣, broken before JA, the word running into the break, the numeral dotted, a trace to the right (GORILA I 265). Sole attestation. Not readable.

LA Zb 1 (bis), a pithos fragment from Larani (Metaxas collection), the group written twice, each time across a damaged area (GORILA IV 86–87). The copie tabulaire dots TI in both groups and the copie normalisée does not. Younger marks TI doubtful in both and notes that the first group sets TI-KU above TU, so that it reads JA-TI-KU-TU or JA-TI-TU-KU (Younger, Linear A Texts). Not readable.

GORILA IV 28–29: ] JẠ-Ụ-P̣A-ṂA-Ị-DA [·] DI[, one string with no divider, five of six signs dotted, broken before JA, sign 4 drawn as MA and as a triangle, one lost sign after DA, line 1 vestiges only. If the signs hold, PA-MA-I-DA = bamat ʾIdā 'high place of Ida' (PS *bVmVt-, Ug. bmt, Heb. bāmâ), Ida word-final only if the lost sign after DA opens a new word (cf. PK Za 17, PK Za 18). JA-U is either JA ending a word lost at the break with U = u- 'and', or vocative yā + u-, which is unparalleled. Not readable.
SY Za 5 ]-MI-JA · JA-WA-PA₃-[, broken after PA₃, the word running into the break (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PE Zb 7 b, on a pithos beside a handle: JA-WA-?, the third sign PI in RILA-S1 (p. 112), VIR in Younger, not decided on the photographs; a tall stroke with a hooked foot follows, not clearly a numeral. No reading.
HT80 .1 ]JU-RA, broken before, on a tablet broken above and below (GORILA I 127). Sole attestation. Not readable.
Karnava & Nikolakopoulou (SMEA 47, 220–21) read THE Zb 13 as 77-08-41-[[?-?-04]]: KA doubtful (Olivier: numeral 100), SI tentative, two signs lost in a clay distortion, TE half-erased. Not readable.
KN Wc 3 ]KA-I-?[, broken both sides, the third sign unidentified (GORILA II 84). Not readable.
KN 22a .2 ]KẠ-JE-[, broken on both sides, KA dotted, the word running into the break after JE. The note allows a further dotted sign after JE (GORILA I 261). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT6a .4–.5 KA-PA-QE 5 ¾, KA at the end of .4 after O-RA₂-DI-NE 2, PA-QE at the head of .5, all three signs whole and undotted (GORILA I 13). The tablet opens .1 KA-PA ·, a repetition that does not establish QE as a suffix or identify the entry. Sole attestation. No reading.
PK 1 .1 KA-QA 2, after SI-[·]-NE-TI 1, the only entry on the tablet with 2 (GORILA I 281). GORILA prints QA undotted, Younger underlines it as doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). No reading.
HT139 .3 ]KA-RA₂, broken before, on a tablet broken below (GORILA I 235). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KE 1 .1 KA-SẠ[, SA dotted, broken after (GORILA I 254). KA-SA may be the start of a longer word: KA-SA-RU (HT 10b). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT Wa 1027 is a nodule with KA on face α and SI on face γ, one sign to a face (GORILA II 9). Wa 1028, on the same page, has SI on α and KA on γ, so the faces give no reading order, and the listed KA-SI and SI-KA are one pair of marks joined two ways. Not a word.

KN Ze 45, four signs on a lost block of the Isopata Royal Tomb, read 77-41-08-04 by Owens (Minos 25/26, 367–69). Wheel, trident, double axe and branch are the standard masons' marks, and Younger, citing Hood, takes them as such (Younger, Linear A Texts). Not a word.

HT63 .1 KA-TI 1, both signs whole and undotted, between *305 · TE 1 and SU-PU₂, which ends against the tablet's whole upper right corner, bracketed open in GORILA's normalized line (GORILA I 118–119). Sole attestation. No reading.
GORILA IV 14–15 reads KN Za 19 .1 ]-KE-JU-MI[, broken at both ends and followed by a separate lost sign. Not readable.
GORILA IV 15 reads KN Za 19 .2 ]*118-MI-NA, written right to left and broken at its start. Not readable.

KN Ze 49, three signs on a Knossos building block known only from Hood's drawing, which Hood reads as masons' marks; the middle sign is not drawn in the SI form, and the staggered layout leaves the order open. Owens reads KE-SI-TE and equates it with MA Ze 11 QE-SI-TE. Outside GORILA and Younger. No reading.
HT27a .4–5 ]KI-*310 · KU-*305̣[, KI at the end of .4 after a break with a trace before it, *310 at the head of .5 (GORILA I 49). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT27a .4 KI-DA-[, after QE 21, the word running into a break after DA. GORILA's note prefers KI-DA-TẸ[ to KI-DA-RỌ[ (GORILA I 49). KI-DA is the start of a longer word. Not readable.
HT 31 .4–5 KI-DE-MA-*323-NA[ ]vest., before *402-VS 400: the word runs into vestiges at the start of .5 (GORILA I 59). Gordon read ki-de-ma-pi-na, taking *323 as PI. Not readable.
HT54a .3 ]KỊ-MỊ-RẠ₂[, broken on both sides, all three signs dotted (GORILA I 105). Sole attestation. Not readable.
TY 2 .2 *309B-[·]-KI-PU 50, the first sign set above *309B lost, only vestiges in the drawing (GORILA I 324–325). Not readable.
ZA 1a .1–2 KỊ-RẸ-ZẠ · NỊ 42 ∠, after *516 ·, all three signs dotted on both copies (GORILA I 333). Younger marks the same three as doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 29 .4–5 [·]-KI-TA 2 in a list of names, a sign lost before KI (GORILA I 55). Not readable.

KH 105, the lower left corner of a tablet: the editors read three partly fragmentary signs AB 45-67-37[, DE-KI-TI[, broken at the right (Del Freo, Rapport 2016–2021, 102, citing Andreadaki-Vlazaki & Hallager 2018, 36–37). KI-TI drops the DE. Not a word.

TY 3a .6 KO-A-DU-WA [OLE] 7 and a fraction, the four signs whole and undotted at the head of the line, OLE restored. .5 breaks off after its numeral, and GORILA's tabular copy sets ] before the word (GORILA I 327). Sole attestation. No reading.
The end of KU-[?]-KO-E (GORILA III 29). Not a word.
Complete, HT 117a lines 7–8: KO-SA-I-TI 1 in a list of names each with 1, between KU-KU-DA-RA and DA-MI-NU, I dotted (GORILA I 197). Not readable.
HT27a .5 KU-*305̣[, after KI-*310 and a divider, *305 dotted, broken after (GORILA I 49). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 18a .1 DA-RE-KU[ ]vest. · KU-*321 · GRA+PA 2 ZZ, KU-*321 undotted between two dividers (GORILA III 191). *321 has no resolved value. No reading.
HT 122a, after KU-RO 31: KU-DA 1, the one unit that brings the two faces to PO-TO-KU-RO 97 (HT 122b; 31 + 65 + 1). A counted entry. No reading.
ZA 14 .3 KU-PỊ 1, PI dotted on both copies, between QA-TI-JU 8 and TU-MI-TI-ZA-SE (GORILA III 181). Younger underlines PI (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT115b .4 KU-TA[, broken after TA, at the end of the last written line (GORILA I 191). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT64 .1 ]KU-ZU-NA, broken before with a trace at left, on a tablet broken above (GORILA I 119). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT6a .3 MA-*321 at the end of the line after JA+RU and two fraction signs, both signs whole and undotted, its 10 at the head of .4 (GORILA I 13). *321 has no resolved value. Sole attestation. No reading.
]-MA-I[ on IO Za 13, traces of a sign before MA (Karetsou, Godart & Olivier, Kadmos 24, 1985, 144). Not a word.
ZA 9 .5 [·]-MA-JU *21F 2, a sign lost before MA (GORILA III 167). MA-JU is the end of a longer word, and KU-MA-JU (HT 20) ends the same way. Sole attestation. Not readable.
PH 30 .2 MA-RE-RỊ-MI-DẸ[, RI and DE dotted, broken after DE. The editors' note offers MA-RE followed by two unread signs (GORILA I 317). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT128a .4 MA-RI, after the numeral 4, both signs whole and undotted at the end of the last line, above inf. mut. GORILA's tabular copy sets [ after the word (GORILA I 221). Sole attestation. No reading.
TY Zg 1 ]MẠ-RỤ-A, broken before MA, MA and RU dotted (GORILA IV 170). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT5 .2 ]MẠ-SI 30[, broken before, MA dotted, the numeral broken after (GORILA I 11). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KN 22c .1 ]MẠ-SỤ-MỊ ·, broken before MA, all three signs dotted, a divider after MI, then [·]-NA[ (GORILA I 261). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH90 .2 MẠ-TA-RI-TẠ[, MA and the second TA dotted, broken after, below [·]-JA[ (GORILA V 43). Sole attestation. Not readable.
PH 15a ]MA-TE-RE *339 1̣1̣[, broken before MA, TE written over an erasure, the numeral dotted and broken after (GORILA I 305). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PK 1 .8 MẠ-TẸ-TI 1, MA and TE dotted on both copies, the editors not excluding MA-DA-TI (GORILA I 281). Younger marks the same two as doubtful and gives MA-DA-TI as the alternative (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PK 1 .7 MA-TI-ZA-I-TE 1, whole and undotted, in a roster of names each counted 1 (GORILA I 281). Amorite MATI+ (Gelb nos. 4568, 4570, 4571, 4573) with zayt "olive", which no held onomasticon uses in a name; or Hurrian mat- (NPN 233–234: Matip-tešup, Mat-teja) with -te, which leaves ZA-I unread. Sole attestation. No reading.
PK Zb 25 MI-DA-RA, the only word on a jar handle, RA marked doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KH79+89 .1 ]MI-NA[, signs undotted, broken on both sides (GORILA V 39). MI-NA stands inside longer words: KU-MI-NA (HTWc3014), A-KU-MI-NA and A-DU-KU-MI-NA (ZA10a), U-MI-NA-SI (HT28b, HT117a). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 23 .2 MI-RE[, no break before MI, broken after RE, below TE-TE-[ (GORILA III 201). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT 117a: MI-RU-TA-RA-RE 1, intact, in the roster under MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO, between U-DI-MI and TE-JA-RE. Written with TA; with DA, MI-RU-DA-RA-RE would be Mīru-darāre 'young bull of freedom' (mīru + √d-r-r, cf. DU-RA-RE). No reading.
HT61 .1 ]MỊ-TỊ · GRA+KU 6, broken before, MI and TI dotted, the numeral partly dotted, a horizontal stroke above ]MI in the editors' note (GORILA I 115). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT78, a single line, ]MU-*312[, broken on both sides (GORILA I 127). Sole attestation. Not readable.
GORILA I 231 reads HT 135a .3 NA-*21F-NE[, broken after NE. Not readable.

HT115a .2–.3 NA-*21F-NE-MI-NA 1, NA-*21F at the end of .2 after the erased ⟦*301-Ụ-RA⟧, NE-MI-NA at the head of .3, all five signs whole and undotted, before SE-KU-TU ½, on a palimpsest (GORILA I 189). Sole attestation. No reading.
KN Zb 20 ]NA-A-PA₃, broken before NA with a dotted trace at the break (GORILA IV 77). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT97a .4 NA-TI 4, both signs whole and undotted, between DI 4 and MA-DI 5̣ in the KA-RU personnel list (GORILA I 159). Sole attestation. No reading.

TY 3a .1–2: GORILA prints NE at the end of .1 and, at the head of .2, the oil vase ligatured with KI, its top lost, with a dotted 5 (GORILA I 327). Younger reads NE · KI+[ ] 5 (Younger, Linear A Texts). NE stands alone and KI belongs to the logogram. Not a word.
GORILA I 231 reads HT 135a .1 ]NẸ-MI-NA 10[: broken before NE, NE dotted. Not readable.
PK 1 .1 SI-[·]-NE-TI 1, one group with a sign lost between SI and NE (GORILA I 281). NE-TI is the end of that group. Not a word.

entries.translation_label: hapax — possibly a personal name; investigated as nūn 'fish' (√n-w-n) but phonetics NI-JA-NU do not map cleanly to /nūn/
entries.note: NI dotted in one of GORILA's two transcriptions (IV 121). Not readable.
PK 1 .6 NI-MỊ 1, MI dotted, between RA-NA-TU-SU 1 and TỤ-SU 1 (GORILA I 281). Younger marks MI as doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KN Wc 26, a roundel (CMS X 120), RU-JA on face a and NI-PI on face b, one disc impression (GORILA II 85). Intact and undotted. Younger enters face b in the logogram column (Younger, Linear A Texts), and NI alone is the fig logogram, but the function of NI-PI is unestablished. No reading.
Both signs dotted (GORILA I 41). Not readable.
ARKH 4a .1 ]-NI-TẠ[, broken both sides, TA dotted (GORILA III 13). Not readable.
HT 154ja .2 ]NỤ-RẸ[, broken at both ends, both signs dotted; GORILA allows ]NU-TE[ (GORILA I 247). Not readable.
HT40 .1 NU-DU-*331 · TE · GRA 207, all three signs whole and undotted, heading the tablet (GORILA I 77). *331 has no resolved value. Sole attestation. No reading.
PK Zc 13 ]-NU-RỊ-JA[, broken on both sides, the word running into the break before NU, RI dotted (GORILA IV 127). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KN Ze 56, on architecture: O-DA against damaged surface after DA, so the word may run on. Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 27 .2 Ọ-MI[, after ]DI-KI 2, O dotted and written over an erasure, KU not excluded for it, broken after MI (GORILA III 205). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT6a .4 O-RA₂-DI-NE 2, all four signs whole and undotted, after the 10 of MA-*321 and before KA-PA-QE (GORILA I 13). Sole attestation. No reading.
ZA 5a .2–3 O-TA-NI-ZA-SẸ 6, SE dotted on both copies, after KI-NI-MA 7 (GORILA III 153). Younger marks SE as doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
PK 1 .5 O-TẸ-JẠ 1, TE and JA dotted on both copies, alone between rulings (GORILA I 281). Younger marks both as doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 93a .6–7 O-TI-[·] 3, a sign lost after TI (GORILA I 147). Not readable.

HT43 .1–.2 PA-*342-I, PA at the end of .1 after MA-SI-DU ·, *342-I at the head of .2, all three signs whole and undotted, then · I GRA+PA 5̣[ (GORILA I 83). *342 has no resolved value. Sole attestation. No reading.
KH 104 .1 SE · GRA · A707 · PA-*47[, *47 at the right break; DA-RE opens .2 (Hallager & Andreadaki-Vlazaki 2017, 283, fig. 4). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH79+89 .3 ]-PẠ-DA-NI, PA dotted, the hyphen after the left break marking a sign lost before PA, a blank after NI before the break (GORILA V 39). Sole attestation. Not readable.

TY 2 .2–3: PA ends line 2 and DA opens line 3, then *309 with RU written above it, JU, KI and 100; the tabular copy sets the six signs as one entry with no divider (GORILA I 325). Every other syllabic entry on the tablet opens with *309, so PA-DA stands before a *309 entry and is not set off as a word. Linear B pa-da[ (DMic II) is broken after. Not a word.
HT104 .3–.4 PẠ-DẠ-SỤ-TỊ 29, PA and DA dotted at the end of .3, SU and TI dotted at the head of .4. GORILA's note does not exclude PA-RO for PA-DA (GORILA I 171). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 73 .2 ]1 PA-I-KI[, broken after (GORILA I 117). Not readable.
HT4 .2 PẠ-RE, after DU-RỊ-TE 2̣, PA dotted (GORILA I 9). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KH 99, published as KH 98, .1 ]PA-RI-DE [[•]], on a fragment from the upper right corner of a tablet, the break before PA and an erased sign after DE (Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, 10–11, Fig. 3). The editors find no parallel for the group and note unusual forms of RI and DE. Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT24a .4 PA-SA-RI-JA ·, all four signs whole and undotted at the head of the line, before the wool ligature MA+RU-MẸ[ (GORILA I 43). It heads the second section as KU-PA₃-RI-JA Kubariya heads the first on .1: a gentilic heading in -iya, RI the stem's last consonant. The stem Pasar- has no Linear A parallel; KH 10 I-PA-SA-JA is another word. Rival: Ugaritic bṣr, Baṣiru, a town of the kingdom, ethnic bṣry (DULAT 240), with PA for b. Sole attestation. No reading.
KH79+89 .2 ]PA-TA · A-RA-[, broken before PA, signs undotted (GORILA V 39). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 6b .4 PA-ZA-[, below the ruling, the word running on into the break. The editors find none of KA, QE or MA satisfactory for the next sign (GORILA III 159). Sole attestation. Not readable.

MIL Zb 2, a clay vessel from Miletos, the only word. The sherd breaks at the right through the second sign, which keeps too little to identify, and the word may run on (photograph and facsimile). Younger gives MIL Zb 1 alone and reports the other Miletos texts unpublished (Younger, Linear A Texts). Not readable.
TY 3b .2 PI-KU-ZU OLE+KI 4, then a second oil entry (GORILA I 329). Intact, no dots. An oil recipient, after KI-RI-SI on .1. No reading.
ZA 21a .2 ]PI-MU 40, broken before PI (GORILA III 195). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH86 .2 PI-NU-[, after a CYP entry, signs undotted, the hyphen before the break marking a group that went on (GORILA III 101). Sole attestation. Not readable.
PH 19 .1 PỊ-Ọ[, both signs dotted, broken after, inf. mut. (GORILA I 309). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ARKH 4a .4–5 PI-TI-NE-A-[, broken after (GORILA III 13). Not readable.
KN 22b ]PỌ-DI-PẠ₃ 1̣10, broken before PO, PO and PA₃ dotted, the hundreds dotted (GORILA I 261). Sole attestation. Not readable.

VRY Zb 2, a fragmentary cup base from the Vrysinas sanctuary (Rethymnon Museum Π 24906), with one or two signs incised on the outer surface. The report gives the editors' readings ]AB 34-31[ or ]AB 11-31[, that is ]*34-SA[ or ]PO-SA[, broken on both sides, after an earlier ]AB 73[ (Del Freo, Rapport 2016–2021, 107). RILA-S1 lists it among its doubtful inscriptions (D 17). Not readable.
HT139 .1 ]-PU-MA-KU, broken before with the word running into the break (GORILA I 235). PU-MA-KU is the end of a longer word. Not readable.

ZA 14 .2 PU-NI-KA-*363 3, after *21F-*118 1, KA written smaller, which GORILA takes as added afterwards (GORILA III 181). *363 has no resolved value (Younger transcribes it SO, Younger, Linear A Texts). No reading.

More exactly PU-*131A, traditionally normalized PU-VIN. It heads allocation sections on HT14 and HT123+124a. The second sign belongs to the VIN/*131A family, and the group behaves as a heading. No reading.
Incomplete: QA-*305-[?], QA and *305 dotted, a further sign lost (GORILA IV 95). Not readable.
HT111a .3 ]QẠ-QA-RU 8, broken before, the first QA dotted (GORILA I 181). The group is QA-QA-RU, whole on HT93a, HT118 and HT122b (.3–4, GORILA I 209). Not readable.
HT111a .2 QA-SẠ-[, after QE-KA 8, SA dotted, the word running into a break. The editors rate QA-RẸ-[ practically as good (GORILA I 181). QA-SA is the start of a longer word. Not readable.

SY Za 10, a serpentine libation table from Syme (HM 5531, MM IIIB–LM IA), the signs shallowly scratched on the rim. Younger prints QA-SA-RA-KU with KU marked doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 15a .2 QE-SI-ZU-E 57; ZA 4a QE-SI-ZU-E 4. On both tablets it precedes *28B-NU-MA-RE and SI-PI-KI in the same run of entries. No reading.
HT58 .1 QẸ-TI-RA-DU · VIR+[?][, QE underdotted in both copies, and GORILA's note allows KẠ-TI-RA-DU (GORILA I 113). Heading of the tablet. Not readable.
KH60 .1 ]RA-KI-TA-NA-SI[, signs undotted, broken on both sides (GORILA III 83). The same five signs stand inside A-KA-RA-KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE… (PEZb3). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 11a .2 ]-RA-MA-SI, broken before, with traces of two signs before RA and MA reworked from another sign (GORILA III 173). RA-MA-SI is the end of a longer word. Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 47b .1 ]RA-NA-RE[, room for one sign before and broken after (GORILA I 91), cf. A-RA-NA-RE (HT 1). Not readable.
PK 1 .6 RA-NA-TU-SU 1, before NI-MỊ 1, written over an erasure (GORILA I 281). Intact. No reading.
PH 2 .1–2 RA-O-DI-KI 60, RA at the end of .1 and O-DI-KI at the head of .2 (GORILA I 288–289). Intact and undotted. No reading.
HT122a .1 ]RA-RI · U-DE-ZA 2̣[, broken directly before RA (GORILA I 207). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT113 .1 RA-RI-DE[, broken after DE (GORILA I 185). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 49a .1 ][·]-RA₂-DỤ[, the first sign lost and the word broken after DU (GORILA I 93). Not readable.

MIL Zb 4, a clay vessel from Miletos, the only word. The sherd is broken below: the first sign keeps a stem and one curved arm, the other side in a worn patch, and the second only an angle at the broken lower right (photograph and facsimile). Younger gives MIL Zb 1 alone and reports the other Miletos texts unpublished (Younger, Linear A Texts). Not readable.

KH 97a: the editors print .1 ]RE · A-JA[ and .2 ]NẠ[, the end of one group, a divider, a group broken at the right, and one dotted sign on the next line (Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007, 8–9, Fig. 2). A-JA[ may begin a longer word; A-JA stands whole on PE Zc 4 and SY Za 2. Not readable.
HT Wc 3012 side b RE-RO, whole and undotted, with ZU-DI-RA on side a (GORILA II 75). Roundel. KA-RE-RO stands alone on HT Wc 3003 (GORILA II 72). No reading.

THE Zb 14 (formerly THE Zb 15), a graffito on a lamp base from Akrotiri, published by Tzachili and Karnava (Minos 39, 2016). The report gives the reading AB 09-A 332 2, that is SE-*332 2, and states that doubts still weigh on it (Del Freo, Rapport 2016–2021, 105–106). RILA-S1 lists it among its doubtful inscriptions (D 15). Not readable.
HT37 .2 RE-SU[, broken after SU, vestiges further right (GORILA I 71). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT125b .3 ]RẸ-TA₂ GRA+PA 20, broken before, RE dotted (GORILA I 215). Sole attestation. Not readable.

HT146 .3 RI-*305 30, whole and undotted (GORILA I 241). Second entry of a list of 30s: ]QẸ[ ]30, RI-*305 30, MA 30, RI-KA-TA 30. *305 holds only a CANDIDATE syllabic value (ḏa, with da live). No reading.

GORILA I 319 prints .4 [·] 1̣ [·]-RU-MA-TI *21M, the first sign lost (facsimile I 318). SigLA reads a worn vertical there as ri (AB53), with no trace of RI's hook. The word stands in a personal-name position receiving OVISm on PH(?)31b. Cf. RI-RU-MA (HT118). Not readable.
KH 6 .4 RI-TA-JE CYP+D[, after ]CYP+[ ] J and before the break (GORILA III 27). Intact, no dots. A cyperus recipient. -TA-JE also ends *306-TA-JE (ARKH Zc 8). No reading.

HT115a .1–2 RỊ-TẠ-MẠ, all three signs underdotted in both copies, followed by NU-WI 2 on .2, on a palimpsest tablet (GORILA I 189). The copie tabulaire joins RỊ-TẠ-MẠ-NU-WI, and GORILA's note on .2 allows a divider before NU-WI, which gives RỊ-TẠ-MẠ and NU-WI. Not readable.
THE 8, an Akrotiri tablet admitted by RILA-S1, listed as RO-A559-A534C 200. The Akrotiri tablets in Younger's transcription print no such sequence (Younger, Linear A Texts). No reading.

HT26b .2 ]-RO-NI 3, broken before with the word running into the break (GORILA I 47). GORILA's note gives two possible forms for the lost sign before RO. RO-NI is the end of a longer word. Not readable.
ZA 9 .3 ]RỌ-SI-RA, broken before RO, RO dotted, at the end of the line, its ideogram and 4̣ after the break that opens .4 (GORILA III 167). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KN Wc 26, face a of a roundel, opposite NI-PI on face b (GORILA II 85). Intact and undotted. RU-JA recurs inside I-RU-JA (HT 7a) and RU-JA-TA-DI (HT Wc 3008). No reading.
HT Wc 3008 side b RU-JA-TA-DI, whole and undotted, with WA-DI-NI on side a (GORILA II 74). Roundel. No reading.
ARKH 2 .6 RU-MỊ-[, MI dotted, broken after, the word running into the break, the end of the line written over an erasure (GORILA III 7). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KN 2 .1 ]RU-NA 2, broken before RU (GORILA I 259). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT25a .2 RU-NI 1, both signs whole and undotted at the head of the line. .1 breaks off after DỊ-NẠ-Ụ[, and GORILA's tabular copy sets ] before the word (GORILA I 45). Sole attestation. No reading.

HT29 .4 SA-*323-MI 1, on a tablet written over an erasure (GORILA I 55). The copie normalisée prints the middle sign whole, the copie tabulaire underdots it and draws it differently. Entry between ]DI-JA-I 2 and [·]-KI-TA 2. *323 has no value. No reading.
HT53a .1 ]SẠ-NẸ[, broken on both sides, both signs dotted, traces at left (GORILA I 103). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT16 .4 SA-PỌ, PO underdotted and written over an erasure, last entry of the tablet (GORILA I 33). GORILA's note gives SA, divider and fraction E as the weaker alternative. Not readable.
KN 32b .2 ]-SẠ-PU, broken before SA, the word running into the break, SA dotted, a stroke and PA after (GORILA I 265). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 21b .3 SẠ-RỊ[, both signs dotted, broken after RI (GORILA III 197). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 73 .3 ]8 SA-RO-QE[, broken after, traces to the right (GORILA I 117). Not readable.
GO 2 verso .2 SE-SI[, broken after SI (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
PK Zb 19 SE-SI-TẠ[, TA uncertain and broken after, Younger allowing SU or JA for the last sign (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH74 .2 ]SỊ-*805-MI, broken before SI, SI dotted, below ]-SỊ · JA-DA-SU (GORILA III 93). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT123b .4 ]SI-DU, beyond the central lacuna that follows KA-NẠ[, NA dotted. The join with HT 124 leaves the lacuna open (GORILA I 210–213). Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH51 .1 ]SỊ-I-SI 3, broken before the first SI, SI dotted (GORILA III 75). GORILA's apparatus offers ]SỊ-I followed by SI as an ideogram. Sole attestation. Not readable.
KH40 ]SỊ-NA-[, the only line, broken above and below, SI dotted, the hyphen before the right break marking a group that went on (GORILA III 69). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT Zb 161 ]SI-PU [, broken directly before SI, a blank then a break after PU, on a fragment of a large vase (GORILA IV 69). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT49a .5 ]SỊ-RẠ 1, broken before, SI and RA dotted (GORILA I 93). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KN Zf 31 opens with ]SI[ standing alone, then after a gap ]SỊ-ZẠ-NE-*310 · DA-DỤ-MI-NE, SI, ZA and DU dotted (GORILA IV 155). Younger prints the same division (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Broken before SI. Not readable.
HT49a .3 SU-KỊ, after ]-RI 1, KI dotted, at the end of the line (GORILA I 93). Sole attestation. Not readable.

ZA 13 .1 ]-SU-PA-[, below sup. mut., broken on both sides with the word running into both breaks, traces before SU compatible with KU (GORILA III 179). SU-PA is a fragment of a longer word. Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT32 .3 SU-RẸ · 108, RE underdotted in both copies (GORILA I 61). GORILA's note keeps the sign a syllabogram because a divider follows it. Entry under SA-RA₂, followed by DI 65. Not readable.
ZA 8 .3–4 TA-I-NU-MA-PA ∠, after A-RI-NI-TA 1[ ] B B and before MA-KA-I-SE 2 E J (GORILA III 165). Intact. No reading.

entries.translation_label: unread—2-consonant glide skeleton inside chance band; probably a commodity/payer abbreviation on the final fraction line
entries.note: HT Zd 156, last entry TA-JẠ with a fraction broken after it, JA underdotted in both copies and worn in the drawing (GORILA IV 133). Stucco fragment, after two NE entries and two A319 entries. Not readable.
ZA 21a .4 TA-KẸ, after ]TẸ 2, KE dotted, at the end of the line (GORILA III 195). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ZA 21a .6 TA-MA-PỊ, after the numeral 5, PI dotted, at the end of the line (GORILA III 195). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT66 .3 TA-MI[, broken after MI, a trace at right, below .2 TA-[ (GORILA I 121). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PS Za 2 .2 TA-NA-I-*301-TI · [, the first group of the line (GORILA IV 52–55). The listed form drops the last sign of the edition's group, which belongs to the TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU paradigm. Not a word.
HT135b .1 [··]-TA-NE[, two signs lost before TA, broken after. The editors allow [·]-*34̣-TA-NE[ (GORILA I 231). TA-NE is the end of a longer word. Not readable.
ARKH 1a .1 ]TA-PI ·, broken before (GORILA III 3). Not readable.
HT4 .3 ]TA-PI-SI-DI 1, broken directly before TA (GORILA I 9). Sole attestation. Not readable.

entries.translation_label: opaque — PN, toponym, or verbal form
entries.note: KN Zf 31, second row, · TA-SA-ZA · between TI-DI-TE-QA-TI and TA-TE-I-KẸ-ZA-RE in the divided text on a silver dress pin from Mavro Spelio, with no numerals or logograms (GORILA IV 154–155). Intact and undotted. The function of the group on the pin is unestablished. No reading.

entries.translation_label: tentative: tG-stem 'she came' + gazzārē 'heroes' (Ugaritic ǵzr); or compound PN
entries.note: KN Zf 31, second row, TA-TE-I-KẸ-ZA-RE after · TA-SA-ZA · on a silver dress pin from Mavro Spelio (GORILA IV 154–155). KE dotted. Not readable.
KH52 .2 ]TA-U-[, broken before TA, signs undotted, the hyphen before the right break marking a group that went on, below ]vest.[ (GORILA III 75). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PYR Zb 5 ]TẸ-JA[, a sherd broken on all sides, TE uncertain. Younger allows the inscription to be complete and JA whole if the sign is Linear A (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Ferrara, Weingarten and Cadogan read the two signs as Cretan Hieroglyphic 025-056 with the top of the second sign broken off (Ferrara, Weingarten and Cadogan, SMEA NS 2, 2016, 87–88, 95). Sole attestation. Not readable.

KH6 .2 ]-TE-NU-RE[ ][·][, the hyphen after the left break marking a sign lost before TE, broken after RE, NU written over an erasure, traces of signs after RE (GORILA III 27). Sole attestation. Not readable.

entries.translation_label: opaque, six legible signs; no Hurrian name element matches a Teššub- reading
entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver dress pin from Mavro Spelio, · TE-SU-DE-SE-KE-I · between A-WA-PI and A-DA-RA. Legible, no damage, dividers both sides (GORILA IV 155). No reading.
ZA 23 .1 TE-TE-[, below sup. mut. and a ruling, the word running on into the break (GORILA III 201). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PH 13c ] E E ZU TE[ as printed left to right, two fraction signs, ZU, then TE at the right break, without hyphens (GORILA I 303). Younger reads the face retrograde and sets TE and ZU apart in the logogram column (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). GORILA V indexes the signs one by one and leaves grouping and direction to the edition (GORILA V 138). No edition groups TE-ZU. Not a word.

entries.translation_label: opaque — QA-TI ending may relate to √q-ṭ-y 'judge' (cf. QA-TI-JU ZA14)
entries.note: KN Zf 31, second row, A-DA-RA · TI-DI-TE-QA-TI · TA-SA-ZA, on a silver dress pin from Mavro Spelio (GORILA IV 154–155). Intact and undotted. No reading.

HT Zb 162, a clay vessel from Casa VAP published by La Rosa and Pugliese Carratelli (1987), listed in RILA-S1's concordance (p. XXVII): DI, numeral, TI-DU. Photo and facsimile show three units: DI, one clear unit stroke with a possible second (the edition's 3 is not visible), and two signs TI-DU, complete at the right. No reading.
HT 49a line .4 (GORILA I 93): ]vest. · TỊ-DU-NI · 1[, TI dotted, the quantity broken after 1. Not readable.

PE Ws GRA+TI E 1, a nodule in Heraklion (Younger, Linear A Texts). TI is the second element of the ligature GRA+TI, and E follows the logogram. Younger gives no inventory number or publication citation for the piece. Not a word.

HT Zf (HM 767), a gold disc 3.4 mm across on the forehead of a bronze bull from the Piazzale dei Sacelli. Perna reads TI and MA, calls the readings uncertain, considers the vertical stroke between them accidental rather than a divider, reports possible traces of one or two more signs beside an abrasion over the right half, and leaves the script open between Linear A and Linear B (Kanta and Perna 2011, 291–293). RILA-S1 lists the object among its doubtful inscriptions (D 21). LB ti-ma is a man's name at Knossos (KN 317, per Perna). Not readable.
PH 16a .1 ]TI-NA[, broken on both sides, traces to the right (GORILA I 307). Younger prints ]TI-NA-[ (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT 31 .1 [·]-TI-SA · PU-KO · *410-VS[, a sign lost before TI (GORILA I 59). Not readable.
PE 2 .4 TO-ME 1 B, ME marked doubtful, before TO-*49-RE (Younger, Linear A Texts). Sole attestation. Not readable.

PK Zb 26, a clay vessel. On the photograph the third sign is a cross within two long arcs on a stem, not DI. RILA-S1 admits it, and Younger lists PK Zb 26 as unpublished, citing Del Freo and Zurbach 2011, 91, with no text (Younger, Linear A Texts). No reading.
PK Za 16 ]TO-SA · PỤ₂-RE-JẠ ]vest.[, broken before TO (GORILA IV 42). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT154a .1 ]TỤ-ME-PẠ-JẠ, broken before, TU, PA and JA dotted (GORILA I 243, as HT 154A). Sole attestation. Not readable.

ZA 14 .3–4 TU-MI-TI-ZA-SE 45[ ], the largest count on the tablet, a space lost after the numeral (GORILA III 181). Intact. It ends like DU-RE-ZA-SE (ZA 10a, 10b) and O-TA-NI-ZA-SE (ZA 5a), but the shared ending does not establish a base. No reading.
HT112a .2 TU-PA-[, the word running into a break after PA (GORILA I 183). TU-PA is the start of a longer word. Not readable.
HT123+124b .3–4 TU-PA-DI-DA with two fractions, whole and undotted, on a face written over an erasure (GORILA I 213). Entry after *188-DU 10 and before KA-NẠ[ on .4. No reading.

HT 25a .3, after A-RI-NI-TA 1, at the end of the line with no numeral. NU is complete at the preserved right edge, though GORILA I 45 brackets it. .4 opens with ZU-JU-PU₂ 1, so TU-QE-NU-ZU-JU-PU₂ may be one name. No reading.
HT128a .1–2 TỤ-RU-NU-SE-ME GRA+[·] 10, TU underdotted in both copies (GORILA I 221). Entry after *326 · PA-RA ·, before WA-TU-MẠ-RE GRA+KU 12. Not readable.
Incomplete: [?]-TU-SE-SU-KI, the first sign lost and TU dotted (GORILA IV 64). Not readable.

PK 1 .6–7 TỤ-SU 1, TU dotted at the end of .6, SU at the start of .7, after NI-MỊ 1 (GORILA I 281). Younger marks TU as doubtful (Younger, Linear A Texts). TU-SU also closes RA-NA-TU-SU on .6. Sole attestation as a word. Not readable.

HT122a .1 U-DE-ZA 2, whole and undotted, the numeral underdotted (GORILA I 207). First entry after ]RA-RI ·, in a list of names totalled KU-RO 31. The other face has A-RA-JU-U-DE-ZẠ 2 (HT122b .3, GORILA I 209), its last sign underdotted. No reading.
PE 1 .1–2, the heading over KU-PA-RI VIR 5̣0[: Younger prints two groups, U-KA-RE and A-SE-SI-NA (Younger, Linear A Texts). The listed form joins the two. Not a word.
HT58 .4 U-KỊ[, KI dotted, broken after, traces of two or three signs to the right. GORILA's note gives U-SỤ[ as less likely (GORILA I 113). Sole attestation. Not readable.
MA 2c .1 ]-U-NA-NA 3, broken before U, the word running into the break (GORILA I 271). Sole attestation. Not readable.
HT26a .3–4 U-NU-*21F 5[, whole and undotted, the numeral broken after (GORILA I 47). Last surviving entry under the vessel heading, after TA-TI 21 and MI-KI-SE-NA 15. *21F = ha. No reading.

Intact, first word of KH 7b line 2: U-TA-I-SE CYP+D ½[ (GORILA III 31). U-TA-I-SI (KH 16) opens on the break (III 47). Cf. LB u-ta-jo (Killen, Mycenaean Greek, glossary, s.v. u-ta-jo): a Cretan name that may come from another language of the island, possibly an isolate. No reading.
KH 16 ]U-TA-I-SI CYP+D [, broken before U (GORILA III 47). Cf. U-TA-I-SE (KH7b). Not readable.

VRY Zb 3, a kyathos fragment from the Vrysinas sanctuary (Rethymnon Museum Π 24605) with two incised signs. The report gives the editors' readings ]AB 37-04[ or ]AB 10-04[, that is ]TI-TE[ or ]U-TE[, the first sign fragmentary, and records that they do not exclude Cretan Hieroglyphic (Del Freo, Rapport 2016–2021, 107–108). RILA-S1 lists it among its doubtful inscriptions (D 18). Not readable.
HT10b .1 U-TI 1, whole and undotted, on a face written over an erasure (GORILA I 21). GORILA takes the stroke inside TI for palimpsest. First entry, before DA-RE 2 and TA-RI-NA 15. No reading.
ZA 10b .1 WA-*362 2, the first entry of face b, before DU-RE-ZA-SE *131B 5 (GORILA III 171). Intact. *362 has no resolved value. No reading.
HT9b .1 PA₃ · WẠ-JẠ-PỊ-[ ], all three signs dotted, the word running into a lacuna, traces at the line end (GORILA I 19). WA-JA-PI is the start of a longer word. Not readable.
HT Wc 3006 side a WA-O-MI, with RA-*314-RA on side b (GORILA II 73). The transcription prints all three signs undotted, and the drawing marks a worn patch inside O. Roundel. No reading.
PI dotted, surface worn (GORILA IV 94). Not readable.
HT128a .2 WA-TU-MẠ-RE GRA+KU 12, MA underdotted in both copies (GORILA I 221). Not readable.
HT5 .3 ]-WI-DU 10[, broken before with the word running into the break, the numeral broken after (GORILA I 11). WI-DU is the end of a longer word. Not readable.

PH 18a .1 ]WI-JA, broken before WI, traces to the left of WI, above inf. mut. (GORILA I 309). WI-JA may be the end of a longer word. WI-JA-SU-MA-TI-TI (HT Zd 157) opens with the same two signs. Sole attestation. Not readable.

entries.translation_label: WI-JA-SU + MA-TI-TI mattitt(u) 'gift', cut by the HT Zd 155 parallel; the √š-m-ṭ cuts wi-yašmaṭi-ti 'from the release' and wi- 'and' + yašmaṭ 'he releases' need TI-TI to write a geminate
entries.note: HT Zd 157 WI-JA-SU-MA-TI-TI (GORILA IV 135). The cut WI-JA-SU + MA-TI-TI rests on HT Zd 155 NA-MA-MA-TI-TI-A319, the same run before A319. No divider is drawn before MA, but the stucco is worn there (GORILA IV 135). The fraction list is on HT Zd 156, a separate fragment. GORILA's two transcriptions print every sign undotted. No reading.

KH 5 .3 WI-NA-DU · *301̣-NA ·, between VINb+WI 2 and KU-PA-ZU (GORILA III 25). Intact, no dots. Linear B wi-na-to (KN As 604.2, 3) is a place, read Inatos on the south coast (DMic II 432), and Younger rejects the identification (Younger, Linear A Texts). No reading.
GORILA IV 125 reads KN Zc 7 .2 WI-PI-[·], one sign lost after PI, with no divider after it. Not readable.
ZA 9 .6 WI-RA-RE-MI-TE *21F 1, the last entry, after [·]-MA-JU *21F 2 (GORILA III 167). Intact. *21F here is the ewe logogram (Younger's OVISf). No reading.

HT113 .2 WI-SA ·[, both signs whole and undotted at the head of the line, a divider after SA. .1 breaks off after RA-RI-DE[. GORILA's tabular copy sets ] before the word (GORILA I 185), but the drawing and the photograph show the tablet's left edge whole beside WI (GORILA I 184). Sole attestation. No reading.
KH 5 .2 WI-SA-SA-NE CYP+E 2, then VINb+WI 2 (GORILA III 25). Intact, no dots. A recipient of cyperus. WI-SA (HT 113) shares the first two signs. No reading.
HT25b .2–3 WỊ-TE-RO · I-TỊ VIR+[?] 28, the logogram underdotted, WI underdotted in both copies (GORILA I 45). Not readable.
TY 3a .1 ]ZẠ-*321 OLE+KI 15 and a fraction, broken before ZA, ZA dotted (GORILA I 327). Sole attestation. Not readable.
ARKH 4b .5 ZẠ-SỊ-ZỤ[, all three signs dotted, broken after, the numeral ]3 broken before (GORILA III 15). Sole attestation. Not readable.
GORILA III 149 reads .4 [·]-TU-ME-SE 18, the first sign lost after JA-PA 1̣[ at the start of the line. It ends in -SE like DU-RE-ZA-SE (ZA 10a, 10b, ZA 20). Not readable.
GORILA IV 13 reads ][· ·]-JA · [· · ·]-JA · JA-WA-[: JA-WA runs into the break, the opening of a longer word. Possible completions: JA-WA-PA₃ (SY Za 5), JA-WA-PI (PE Zb 7). Not readable.
GORILA I 175 reads HT 108 .3 ][·]-RA₂-TI 10, the first sign lost and joined by a hyphen. GORILA's note offers two candidates, neither secure. Not readable.

GORILA I 23 reads HT 11a .1 A-RU-RA-[·]: the line breaks after RA, a fourth sign is lost (GORILA's note draws two dotted candidates, the second shaped like the SU of A-SU-JA on .4), and RU is written over an erased sign. Line .2 opens ]3, the numeral broken before the 3, so the first entry may exceed 3 and the list can reach KU-RO 10. Not readable.

LACH Za 1, a doubtful right-to-left inscription on a limestone vessel fragment from Tel Lachish, is broken at both ends. RI-DA-U is internally complete between dividers, but the missing context prevents a secure function or meaning. Finkelberg, Uchitel and Ussishkin (1996, 202–203) compare the related ri-da-(wa)-*65 groups around vessel ideogram *309 on TY 2 but leave the term unidentified. No reading.

SY Za 3 is broken on both sides of KA-NA. GORILA V 66–67, before the joins, prints none of the middle (ca. 20 signs lost). From the joins (Muhly & Olivier 2008), Thomas 2020, 20 distinguishes only ]-KA-NA-[. Younger reads ]•-•-•SE-KA-NA-SI[•]TE[ with SE, SI and TE doubtful, and Hogan (quoted by Thomas) ∙ ∙ ∙ -ṢẸ-KA-NA-ṢI-[∙] ṬẸ-[. No divider is printed in the stretch, so no word boundary is known. KA-NA stands in formula position 4, where the other sites have U-NA-KA-NA-SI of √k-n-s. Not readable.

GORILA I 314–15 reads PH 28a .1 A-PA₃-[: A and PA₃ are dotted, and the photograph and drawing show part of a third sign on the broken right edge. The drawing shows the left edge unbroken, with bare clay before A, while GORILA's normalized text prints ]A-PA₃-[. Semitic ʾab 'father' fits the two signs only as a stem. Not readable.

GORILA I 314–15 reads PH 28a .2 ]1̣ JA-KI-PA₃[: a dotted unit stroke opens the line, and a trace follows PA₃ on the broken right edge (GORILA: trace à droite). yakīn-ʾab 'may the Father establish' fits the three signs only as a stem. Not readable.

GORILA I 314–15 reads PH 28a .3 ]1̣ A-RI-JA[: a dotted unit stroke opens the line, and JA sits on the broken right edge, so the end of the word is lost. ʾaryā 'lion' fits the three signs only as a stem. Not readable.
ARKH 1a .5 2 ½ A-PA-[ (GORILA III 2–3): the fraction secures the start, and part of a further sign stands on the broken right edge. Cf. ]A-PA-[ on KN 32a. Not readable.
KN 32a .1 ]A-PA-[ (GORILA I 264–65): A and PA dotted, the top of A in the break, part of a third sign on the edge, and GORILA's note allows ]A-PA-*118[. Cf. A-PA-[ on ARKH 1a. Not readable.

GORILA IV 40 reads PK Za 14b I · JA-SA-SA[: the divider secures the start, and the second SA sits on the broken right edge, its right arm running into the break. JA-SA-SA never stands alone and opens JA-SA-SA-RA-ME wherever the sequence continues (IO Za 6, PS Za 2, TL Za 1, PK Za 27). Not readable.

GORILA IV 40 reads PK Za 14 ]TU-ME̤ I · JA-SA-SA[: the break falls before TU, which is drawn whole, ME is dotted in the second transcription, and I stands across the table's corner with no divider before it, so the group is ]-TU-ME-I. The same signs as TU-ME-I tummī (PK Za 8), with the start lost. Not readable.
PK Za 12 d: A-PA-DU-PA-[, no divider after DU, then a lacuna (Younger). Not readable.
KH 92 .2 ]NA-KI 1 vest.[, broken before NA (Younger). Not readable.

RILA-S1 D 16: TI Zb 1 doubtful; the *301 would be dextroverse and turned 90°, and the second sign recalls CM 1 026. The facsimile shows a chevron and a triangle, neither clearly *301 or SI. Not readable.

GORILA I 42–43 reads HT 24a .1 KU-PA₃-RI-JA · KỊ-MA+RU[: the second sign is the wool ligature MA+RU (A559) that opens every line of the tablet, KI is dotted and was written in after it (note .1), and the ligature sits on the broken right edge, so the end of the group is lost. Not readable.

GORILA I 156–57 reads HT 96a .5 ]KU-MA-RO · TE NI 20: the break runs across the lower left, KU stands partly on its edge, and note .5 records a trace to the left of KU, so the start of the word is lost. The divider after RO secures the end. Not readable.
GORILA I 6–7 reads HT 3 .1 ]DỊ-NẠ-[: both signs are dotted, the line is broken on both sides, and the hyphen after NA runs into the break. Not readable.
GORILA III 80–81 reads KH 59 .3 ]-DỊ-NA 5: the hyphen after the bracket marks the end of a longer word, DI is dotted, and the drawing shows a trace before it in the break. Not readable.

GORILA III 192–93 reads ZA 19 RA-TE-[: a tablet fragment broken at top, bottom and right, the hyphen after TE running into the break. The drawing shows the left edge, and the second transcription prints ]RA-TE-[. Not readable.
GORILA III 29 reads KH 7a .1 ]NẸ-[·]-KI *334 4: broken before NE, NE dotted, one sign lost inside the word, KI written small. Not readable.
GORILA I 127 reads HT 79+83 ]TU-[·] 3: broken before TU, the sign after it lost. Not readable.
GORILA I 231 reads HT 135a .2 ]-MI-TU ·, the hyphen before MI running into the break: the end of a longer word. Not readable.
GORILA I 231 reads HT 135a .2 MI-KA[, broken after KA. Not readable.
GORILA I 91 reads HT 47a .6 ]-MI-NU-MI, the hyphen before MI running into the break: the end of a longer word. Not readable.
GORILA IV 9 reads KN Za 10 b DA-WA-[·]-ḌU-WA-ṬO, one sign lost between WA and DU. The top of the gap is chipped, so a lost divider cannot be excluded. Not readable.

Muhly and Olivier 2008, 211 read •-60-67-•-30-09[: only the foot of the first sign's upright survives (DA, A, ME or SA), with no sign lost to the left. The fourth is perhaps ZU over WA over JA. Broken after SE. Earlier transcriptions omit the fourth sign and read RA-KI-NI-SE. Not readable.

HT 51a .2 TI-NI[, broken after, on a fragment broken on all sides (GORILA I 98–99). TI-NI-TA heads HT 27a. PS *tiʔin- 'fig tree' was the proposed reading; NI 'figs' stands on .1 of the same face. Not readable.
HT 51b .1 ]KU-ME-TA 12[, broken before (GORILA I 98–99), so the word may be longer. Egyptian Kmt 'the black land' was the proposed reading. Not readable.

KH 13 .2 ]A-SE-RE-ZA[, broken before and after on a fragment, all four signs read; .3 *304 (GORILA's 'sans doute') and CYP (GORILA III 42–43). The word may be longer at either end. Cf. ]RE-ZA CYP on KH 86. Not readable.

ARKH 3a .1 ]-KA-NE · GRA[ (GORILA III 9): GORILA's ]- marks loss inside the word, note .1 records a sign trace to the left, and the facsimile shows a stroke before KA. The end of a longer word. Personal name Qanē (√q-n-y) was the proposed reading. Not readable.
HT 51b .2 ]ZU-DU ⅝, broken before (GORILA I 98–99). ZU-DU on HT 99b is a counted list entry. Not readable.
HT 93a .8 PA₃-NI-NA[, broken after (GORILA I 147). It fits PA₃-NI-NA, which opens the first section on .1. Not readable.
HT 47a .4 KI-DA-RO̥[, RO dotted and broken after (GORILA I 91). It fits Qidaru, written whole on HT 117a. Not readable.
HT 27b .1 ]MI-DA, heading the first section, broken before (Younger); the edge is chipped. Not readable.
HT 3 2 QE-RA₂-JA[, damaged after JA (photograph and facsimile); or QE-RI-JA (Younger). PS *qarya- 'city' was the proposed reading. Not readable.
HT 3 SI-TU-RA₂-RE 5, whole at the preserved left edge; or SI-TU-RI-RE (Younger). Šitūl-ēl 'El has planted' needed RE to write /ēl/. No reading.
HT 11b .1 RU-RA₂ after ]DE-NU, heading the KA list; the top of the first sign is damaged, RU or SA (SA-RA₂, Younger). Not readable.

PH 7a .1 DI-PA-JA[, the left edge original, a sign trace after JA at the right break (GORILA I 295, note .1). The word may run on. Pre-Greek *dipas, Linear B di-pa, was the proposed reading. Not readable.

PH 7a .3 ]JA-RU-MA-NE[: the left edge is broken through JA, and the line breaks after NE, where a trace may be a dotted unit stroke (GORILA I 295, note .3). Personal name Yarīmān (√r-w-m) was the proposed reading. Not readable.

ZA 14 .4 JA-WI[, the last group on the line, against the right edge, with no numeral; .5 is lost, ]vest.[ (GORILA III 180–181; Younger JA-WI[). The word may run onto .5. Personal name Yawī (√ḥ-w-y) was the proposed reading. Not readable.

ZA 4a .2-3 JA-TO-JA[ ]3[: the group ends .2 against the right edge, the last JA worn, and the start of .3 before the numeral is damaged (GORILA III 148–149; Younger JA-TO-JA[). The word may run onto .3. Personal name Yaṯūʿaya (√y-ṯ-ʿ) was the proposed reading. Not readable.

PH 7a .4 JA-SỊ-DA-RẠ[, the left edge original: RA dotted in both GORILA transcriptions, SI in the second, and the break cuts into RA (GORILA I 295). Personal name Yaśdara (√s-d-r) was the proposed reading. Not readable.

IO Za 7 (HM 3784, libation table, Iouktas): A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA · JA-TI-*321[, the left end intact, broken after *321 (GORILA V 28–29). The divider is cut over an erased JA. *321 has no value. Not readable.
